title: Attunement (Open Loops)
markdown:
Attunement is the Executive adapting to each person it works with. Its first piece is **open loops**: the concrete things someone on the roster committed to, or was asked for, in conversation — tracked until they're done, and chased when they slip. It lives in `openexecutive.attunement`.

### Why it exists

Before this, commitments were captured only from the principal's own words (`memory.episodic.should_extract` requires `is_principal`), because stored messages did not record who said them. A teammate's "I'll send the vendor quote by Thursday" vanished. And nothing in production ever set `scheduled_actions.awaiting_response_since`, so the nudge engine's commitment-chasing source had nothing to chase.

### Sender attribution and feedback

Every persisted user message records `chat_messages.sender_person_id`: the **resolved** rostered sender, never the session owner. Discord and Telegram sessions from unrostered senders are owned by the principal so they still show in the sidebar; attribution keeps those outsiders' words from ever being read as the principal's. The web route passes its header-resolved caller (a header-less caller is the principal's own CLI / API surface; a signed-in email not on the roster resolves to nobody). Slack, Discord and Telegram pass the sender they resolved. For the turn itself, the Executive records the resolved speaker on `Session.caller_person_id`, which tool handlers read.

Assistant replies can carry explicit feedback: `chat_messages.feedback` (`up` / `down`) via `POST /sessions/{id}/messages/{message_id}/feedback`, restricted to the session's own caller or the principal. The chat stream's `done` event includes `message_id` so the web panel renders 👍/👎 on the reply. Each rating writes an `attunement` audit row.

### Opening and closing loops

After every chat turn whose speaker resolved to a rostered, non-archived person — on any channel, email included, because the hook sits in the Executive rather than an adapter — `schedule_open_loop_pass` runs fire-and-forget, beside the episodic extraction:

1. **Prefilter** — a keyword check ("I'll", "by Friday", "can you", … or, when loops are open, "sent", "done", …) skips most turns with no model call. A turn carrying an attached document (`[Attached: …]` inlined by `integrations.attachments`) is skipped outright: the document's words sit in the same message — after the text on the web, before it on Telegram and Discord — so a quote found there would be the document's, not the speaker's. The short filename note an email or upload leaves in the speaker text is written `(Attached files: …)` precisely so it does not trip this skip — that turn carries no document text.
2. **Budget** — `ATTUNEMENT_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY` (default 200) is taken atomically from the `attunement_usage` row for the UTC day.
3. **One forced-tool call** (`record_open_loops`, routing model) sees today's date, the speaker, the roster, the loops the speaker may close, the message and the reply. It may:
   - open a **commitment** the speaker made (owner = the speaker);
   - open an **ask** the speaker made of a named rostered person (owner = that person);
   - when the principal speaks, open a commitment the principal attributes to a named teammate ("Sara will send the numbers Monday");
   - close loops the speaker reports done, sent, no longer needed or cancelled — their own loops, or any loop when the principal speaks.
4. **Gates in code**, not just the prompt: every item must quote the speaker's own message verbatim — the turn's speaker text (`memory_text` when given: an email's new text without its quoted chain, a briefing handoff's short line), never the framed prompt (commitments through the episodic extractor's `_is_valid_user_commitment`, so the Executive's own suggestions are never logged as someone's promise), and the stored `text` must itself appear verbatim in that message — it is re-injected into the nudge intent a tool-using turn executes, so it is never a model paraphrase (the intent also tells that turn to treat the quoted text as data); owners must resolve to exactly one rostered person (a full name not on the roster never falls back to a rostered first name — "Ben Jones from Acme" is not Ben Ortiz); a teammate cannot attribute a commitment to someone else; the principal's own commitments are left to the episodic extractor (in solo mode only the undated ones — see below); a loop id outside the closable set is ignored; each owner holds at most `ATTUNEMENT_MAX_OPEN_LOOPS_PER_PERSON` (15). Due dates are clamped to 60 days and default to `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_DEFAULT_DUE_DAYS` (2).
5. **Audit** — one `attunement` row per pass (`op=extract`, opened / closed / dropped with reasons) plus `loop_opened` / `loop_closed` rows.

### Storage and chasing

A loop is a `scheduled_actions` row: `kind='open_loop'`, `channel='__internal__'`, inserted already `done` so the runner never dispatches it, `assigned_to_person_id` = owner, `awaiting_response_since` = due time, `scope_key` = `loop:{owner}:{hash}`. A partial unique index over open loops dedupes concurrent passes. That shape is exactly what existing readers expect:

- the nudge engine's commitment source chases an open loop **as soon as it is overdue**, with a check-in addressed to its owner, through `prefer_channel_for`, availability windows, `NUDGE_MAX_PER_SCOPE` and the outbound guard;
- `list_awaiting_replies_by_person` counts it **once it is due** (the same cut-off the nudge engine uses), so `/today`'s roster and reflection's "people waiting" include an overdue loop but not one still in the future — while `last_contact_at_by_person`, the client engagement "follow-ups completed" count and the `/today` activity feed (which now filters `__internal__` rows in SQL so loops cannot crowd real sends out of its window) all exclude it, since a loop is not a message sent;
- `executive_reflection` renders an **OPEN LOOPS** block (up to 10, overdue flagged);
- in solo mode, the morning brief and the `/today` header get a **DUE THIS WEEK** block of the principal's own loops that are overdue or due within 7 days (`open_loops.principal_due_soon`), and the Briefing shows them in a **Due soon** card.

### Solo mode: the principal's dated commitments

In a team install the principal's own commitments are dropped (`principal_commitment`). In solo mode — one person using Open Executive for themselves — nobody else will chase what they promise, so the pass keeps the ones that say when they are due. The turn's pinned mode travels with the pass (`schedule_open_loop_pass(..., workspace_mode=…)`, read from the workspace when absent). Solo swaps the extraction prompt for `_SYSTEM_SOLO` (a separate constant; the team `_SYSTEM` is byte-identical and pinned by a test), which allows a dated commitment of the principal's own and requires its quote to carry the date words. In code, a principal commitment is opened only when the model's `due_date` parses as a real `YYYY-MM-DD` (`_stated_due_date` — never `_resolve_due`'s 2-day default) **and** the quote matches `_STATED_DUE_HINT` (weekday, month, "tomorrow", "end of Q4", "the 14th", "in 3 days", …); anything else is dropped as `principal_commitment_undated` — an undated "I'll look into pricing" is an initiative, not a loop. The loop is owned by the principal, so the nudge engine chases it through their channel once overdue; when no channel reaches them, the brief's DUE THIS WEEK block and the Briefing's **Due soon** card still show it. Asks and contacts' commitments behave exactly as in team mode.

A loop closes (its `awaiting_response_since` cleared, audited) when the owner reports it done, when the principal or owner calls `close_open_loop` or uses **Mark done** on the person's page, when its owner is archived, or when it passes `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_TTL_DAYS` (21) — expired at the start of each nudge scan.

### Who can see and close a loop

What someone owes is not roster-public. `list_open_loops` shows the principal everyone's loops only on a **private surface** — web chat, a Slack or Discord DM, or a 1:1 Telegram chat; in a shared channel or thread, a Telegram group, a Google Chat space or an email thread (which can carry cc's), and for anyone else, it shows only the caller's own loops, and an unresolved caller gets nothing. `GET /people/{id}/open-loops` is the principal's or that person's only.

`close_open_loop` (chat tool) and `POST /open-loops/{id}/close` only close when the resolved caller is the principal or the loop's owner. Every one of these checks, and the feedback route's, goes through one helper, `people.store.is_principal_or_self`. Loop ids appear in prompts and replies and inbound email reaches the Executive, so a quoted "close loop 12" from an unrostered sender, a signed-in web user not on the roster, or an unattended session (a scheduled nudge's prompt quotes the loop text) is refused. The reflection pass is not given the tool at all.

### Outcome ledger — what lands, per person

`attunement.outcomes` records every **proactive** DM to a rostered person and resolves it with no model call, so the Executive can do more of what gets answered and less of what doesn't.

- **Recording.** Proactive work tags itself with `tag_proactive(source, ref)` — a ContextVar, wrapped only around non-yielding code — and the single point every DM passes through, `schedule_tools._record_outbound_context`, writes a `proactive_outcomes` row next to the `outbound_context` linkage when a tag is set and the recipient resolves to a Person. Tagged callers: the scheduler's generic dispatch (a nudge is `nudge_stalled` / `nudge_commitment` / `nudge_initiative`, or `open_loop` when its commitment target is an open loop, keyed by its scope key; anything else is `followup`), `executive_reflection` (`reflection`), `executive_research` (`research`) and alert review (`alert_review`, keyed `alert:<id>`). A user's own chat turn is never tagged, and web-chat sends write no linkage. Only the addressed recipient counts: an email's first rostered `to` address gets a row, its cc's and any other recipients only get reply linkage; and a follow-up the principal scheduled for themselves is not outreach.
- **Resolution.** `replied` when the recipient's reply consumes the linkage (`mark_outbound_context_consumed`). `acted` when the thing it was about got done, however it was done: the open loop a chase was about is reported done **by its owner** (the principal tidying a loop away, or saying someone else's is done, credits nobody); the approval a stalled-run nudge chased is resolved (`resumer.apply_resolution`), credited to the person who resolved it; the initiative a check-in was about gets a real change (a new status or summary, not a re-mention), credited only to the person who made it — an edit through `PATCH /memories/initiatives/{id}`, which carries no caller identity, credits nobody; or the alert a review DM was about is acknowledged or resolved — credited only to the person it is routed to and the principal, never to someone DM'd about it on an earlier pass. `void` when that alert is dismissed, found stale or expires unread: the DM didn't matter, so it counts neither way — a dismissal, which anyone with API access can make, can never lower someone's rate. `ignored` when still open after `ATTUNEMENT_IGNORE_AFTER_HOURS` (72) — swept at the start of each nudge scan and whenever rates are read, so the rates stay honest with the scan disabled. A later `acted` or `void` overrides an earlier `ignored` — the thing can get done days after the sweep, and that verdict is the truer one; a late reply does not. Expired, cancelled or archived loops resolve nothing.
- **Use.** `acceptance()` gives per-(person, source) counts over 30 days. The nudge engine demotes a candidate whose person left their **last** `ATTUNEMENT_MUTE_MIN_SENDS` (5) resolved sends (by send time) of that source all unanswered (`muted_pairs`): it ranks after every other candidate and its cooldown is multiplied by `ATTUNEMENT_MUTE_COOLDOWN_MULTIPLIER` (3). It is never dropped, and a single answer lifts it — judged on the most recent sends rather than a 30-day share, which would keep a demoted source (with fewer chances to be answered) demoted long after the person came back. Reflection gets a **WHAT LANDS** block (per person, per source with ≥3 resolved), and the prompt steers DMs toward the kinds that land. `GET /people/{id}/outreach` (principal or that person) backs a "How they respond" card on the person page.

### Working style — how each person likes replies

`attunement.style` keeps at most four short style rules per person ("lead with the recommendation, then the numbers") and pins them into **that person's own turns** as a `<working_style>` block in the user turn — right after `<current_speaker>`, never a cached system block, and only for a resolved, rostered, non-archived speaker. The block says the current request always wins and that the rules never authorize an action.

- **Evidence.** A background pass (one forced `record_working_style` call) reads the person's last 40 attributed messages, each paired with the reply that answered it and the reaction **they** gave it: 👍/👎 they left themselves (`chat_messages.feedback_by_person_id`, so the principal rating someone's session is not that person's reaction), any note, and replies stopped mid-stream. Every rule must cite that evidence — basis `feedback` needs a cited reply carrying a reaction; basis `stated` needs the person's request quoted verbatim from a cited message. Honcho is not read or written, so this works the same with `HONCHO_ENABLED=false`.
- **Style only.** Rules are validated in code before they are stored or shown: one line of Latin-script text (so look-alike letters cannot hide a denied word), 8–160 characters; a deny-list that rejects action words (send, approve, pay, schedule…), nudges to act without checking (confirm, check, verify, pause, proceed, go ahead, judgment, instinct, trust, decide…), talk about instructions or tools, URLs, handles, amounts, markup, snake_case identifiers and roster names; and an allowlist — the rule must name some aspect of how a reply reads (length, format, tone, detail, what to lead with…). Edits typed on the person page go through the same checks, and every stored rule is checked again each time the block is rendered and when the lock is toggled, so a rule saved under an older, weaker check never reaches a turn. The block is scrubbed with the shared `utils.prompt_blocks.scrub_block_line`, which also backs `<peer_memory>`.
- **Pacing.** The Executive schedules the pass after each attributed turn; it runs once `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_TRIGGER_TURNS` (10) new messages have arrived since the last pass, or right after the person leaves a 👎 on a reply to their own message (`POST /sessions/{sid}/messages/{mid}/feedback`; someone else's rating triggers nothing), with at least 5 messages of history. At most once per `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS` (2) and `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_MAX_PER_DAY` (4) times a day per person, and from the shared `ATTUNEMENT_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY` budget. The slot is claimed with one conditional UPDATE (never under a one-minute interval, and `MAX_PER_DAY=0` means no passes), so concurrent triggers run one pass. The model returns the learned rules in full: a deliberate empty list drops them (newer reactions contradict them), while a malformed call or a list whose every rule fails validation changes nothing.
- **People stay in charge.** `GET/PUT/DELETE /people/{id}/attunement` (the principal or that person) back a "How I work with them" card with edit, lock and reset. Rules typed there are always kept — a pass only fills the remaining slots — and toggling the lock alone (`PUT` without `rules`) keeps the learned rules and their provenance. A locked profile is never rewritten by a pass, a pass never overwrites an edit made while it ran, and an archived person's routes return 404. Every change is kept in `attunement_profile_history`; archiving a person drops both.

### Settings

`ATTUNEMENT_ENABLED`, `ATTUNEMENT_OPEN_LOOPS_ENABLED`, `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_DEFAULT_DUE_DAYS`, `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_TTL_DAYS`, `ATTUNEMENT_MAX_OPEN_LOOPS_PER_PERSON`, `ATTUNEMENT_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY`, `ATTUNEMENT_IGNORE_AFTER_HOURS`, `ATTUNEMENT_MUTE_MIN_SENDS`, `ATTUNEMENT_MUTE_COOLDOWN_MULTIPLIER`, `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_ENABLED`, `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_TRIGGER_TURNS`, `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS`, `ATTUNEMENT_STYLE_MAX_PER_DAY`. The open loops themselves live in `scheduled_actions` and the attribution columns in `chat_messages`, both wiped by company switches and resets; `attunement_usage`, `proactive_outcomes`, `attunement_profiles` and `attunement_profile_history` are wiped with them.

### Known gaps

Email and Google Chat turns open and close loops (the hook is in the Executive) but do not persist `chat_messages`, so they carry no stored attribution or feedback. `POST /alerts/{id}/ack` has no per-caller authorization (pre-existing), which is why a dismissal voids rather than counts against anyone. Principal briefs and dynamic-workflow deliveries run without a chat session, so they write no outreach linkage and are not in the outcome ledger; broadcasts to a channel have no single recipient and are not counted either.
